items.heading: A Political Science Phd
items.text: A political science PhD is not a one-way ticket into a lecture hall. It is a credential in original research, sustained argument, and deep subject command, a credential that genuinely feeds five different career tracks, each with its own pay structure, timeline, and risk.

items.heading: Why This Is a Different
items.text: Why this is a different question than "what can a political science graduate do".

items.heading: The Order Below Follows Real
items.text: The order below follows real growth and growth headroom as you gain reputation and proof, not which title sounds most respectable at a family gathering. The tracks with real ownership or an uncapped pay structure come first; the tracks locked to a fixed government or UGC scale come last, regardless of how prestigious they sound.

items.heading: You Have Already Spent 4
items.text: You have already spent 4-7+ years and cleared UGC-NET/JRF, a fresh graduate is choosing whether to start that; you are choosing what to do with it now that it is done.

items.heading: You Can Enter a Think
items.text: You can enter a think tank at Fellow or Senior Fellow level, not the entry research-associate rung most fresh graduates start at.

items.heading: Ad
items.text: Ad-hoc and guest-faculty pay, and the wait for a permanent post, are a real near-term reality specific to people who have already finished a PhD, not a hypothetical future problem.
